text: Education in Poland is structured with compulsory education beginning at age 6 or 7, and a significant reform in 2017 extended primary school from 6 to 8 years, eliminating the previous middle school (gimnazjum) system. The new structure includes eight years of primary education (grades 1–8), followed by upper secondary education. Upper secondary education offers general academic programs (liceum) leading to the Matura exam for university admission, vocational training through technical schools (technikum) or basic vocational schools (zasadnicza szkoła zawodowa), and specialized programs for students with disabilities. Tertiary education follows the Bologna system, featuring a three-year bachelor's degree followed by a two-year master's degree, with some programs lasting longer (e.g., five to six years for medicine or pharmacy). The grading system at the university level uses a numeric scale from 2 to 5, with 3.0 being the minimum passing grade. Foreign language education is a key component, with students required to learn two foreign languages, typically English and another language, starting in lower secondary school. The education system has undergone major reforms, including a shift from a 10-year to an 11-year compulsory education structure, and a reorganization of the curriculum to emphasize modern skills and reduce rote learning. The system emphasizes national identity, history, and civic education, with a strong focus on preparing students for higher education and the workforce. There is also a growing emphasis on inclusive education and support for students with special needs.
